hook: A purple raspberry stuck to flypaper in a Ukrainian hardware store turns out to be very talkative. Most of the page is that voice telling its own history in transcribed documents, and it is funnier and stranger than the dry opening suggests. Pay attention to what it does and does not understand about where it has ended up.
whyItMatters: Tagged absurdism and pattern-screamer, it delivers cosmic-scale backstory through a narrator who is both godlike and hopelessly confused. The gap between universe-sized claims and a cheap sticky trap is the engine of the whole piece.
thingsToNotice:
The early tests set the tone with deadpan absurdity: one D-class is stretched thin and pulled in, another is replaced by a croissant, and a squirrel scrambles the researchers' minds. Then the interview lands its best line, "Who is flies?", from a thing that has consumed entire universes and still has no idea what a fly is.

The transcribed documents show its civilization rising to a hive of uploaded near-gods that found God hiding as a hawk-shaped thing, hurt it until it gave in, and absorbed its knowledge. The pattern-screamer element arrives through screaming, laughing watchers it senses beyond Limbo. In the last document it finally catches a glimpse of a raspberry in a researcher's head, hears the researchers thinking of it as food, insists that they are the real fruit of knowledge, and declares that it understands everything. The addendum then shows a primate-like mouth with black eyes growing out of its own center, circling the cell and lunging back at it; the cameras die, and afterward the object is simply gone, which makes its last boast land as bitter irony.
